turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr. Iyer, kindly sit down. I will check your blood pressure, pulse, temperature and oxygen before doctor calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you sister. I am quite anxious, this cough is not leaving me and I keep thinking the pressure is out of control.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Please relax your arm. Blood pressure is one hundred and fifty six over ninety four, pulse eighty four, temperature thirty six point eight, saturation ninety seven percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): One fifty six over ninety four? That is high only. What to do now.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, sit quietly, getting tense will not help. Let doctor decide.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good morning. I am Dr. Shah. You have come with your daughter. The nurse has noted the pressure. What is the main problem today?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, the dry cough. It has been going on for weeks. I caught a cold, sneezing and running nose, that part settled, but I feel the cough is still from that cold.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He keeps saying cold, but the bad coughing started after they gave the new tablet. It has been nearly a month of cough.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Not a month, about three weeks. Cold was first. Ramipril I began later, ten days ago or maybe two weeks, I cannot date it properly.

[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Cough about three weeks by your account, nearly a month by your daughter's, you link it to a cold that has settled, and the ramipril start date is unclear, somewhere in the last two weeks. Is that fair?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes doctor, that is fair. The nose is fine now, no running nose anymore.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is there any phlegm, or is it a dry cough?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Dry. Mm, I suppose a tiny bit sometimes, not really phlegm.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever at present, or pain in the chest?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): My elder brother is on lisinopril, same family of tablet, for years, and he never coughs. He is fine at sixty seven. So why should I get it?
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): We can talk about your brother's lisinopril in a minute. First, do you have fever or chest pain now?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no fever and no chest pain. I am sure of that.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He gets short of breath on the stairs, I have watched him stop and hold the rail.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not. I am not breathless. The knees pain on stairs, that is why I stop. She is mistaken.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Noted. You deny breathlessness and describe knee pain on the stairs, while your daughter reports breathlessness. I will keep both versions. Do you smoke?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I walk every morning, doctor, forty minutes, but the dust on the road is terrible these days, that also irritates the throat I feel.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Walking is good, we will put that down. I did ask about smoking though. Do you smoke, or did you ever?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never smoked. I don't like it.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze, a whistling when you breathe?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No whistling.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does the cough wake you at night?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose, sometimes, not really. I sleep most of the time.
[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): I will not call it a night-time cough then, since you are not sure. Which tablets are you on for the blood pressure?

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five milligram every morning, for years. Ramipril five milligram once a day, the new one. And the water tablet, that small white one, also every morning, for the pressure. I don't know the proper name of the water tablet.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And Crocin when his head pains. Not daily.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): One Crocin, five hundred milligram, only if the headache comes, once or twice a week maybe. The headache is not severe, just a dull pain sometimes, since the pressure has been up.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): No diabetes medicines?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I don't have sugar, no sugar tablets.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): How regularly are you taking the ramipril, the five milligram once a day?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose I do. Sometimes in the morning rush I miss it, I cannot say I never miss. Most days yes.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies? Rash, swelling, breathing difficulty with a medicine?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies at all.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There was an antibiotic, years back, red rashes on the body. He stopped that antibiotic and avoided it. Neither of us remembers the name.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not accept that. I have no memory of any rash. No allergy.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): I will record that you deny any allergy, and your daughter recalls a rash to an unnamed antibiotic in the past. It stays disputed. Let me examine you now.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Throat is mildly red. Lungs are clear with no wheeze or crackles, heart sounds are normal with no murmur, and the ankles are not swollen.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Mildly red throat means infection? Is it serious? Will I need antibiotics? I am frightened of antibiotics if that old story is true.

[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): A mildly red throat with a clear chest does not mean a serious infection, and I am not starting an antibiotic. Putting it together, this may be a cough from ramipril, or the remaining effect of the cold. I cannot say which for certain, so I am not giving you a firm diagnosis.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): If you are not sure, must we change the tablet? If I stop ramipril my pressure may jump. It is already one fifty six over ninety four. What is the alternative?

[SEG0045] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, I still want to change it, because if the ramipril is responsible the cough should ease after stopping, and if it does not we will look again. Please stop ramipril from today. Start telmisartan forty milligram once every morning. Keep taking amlodipine five milligram and the water tablet as before.

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Telmisartan forty, morning. Is it safe with the water tablet? Will this one also cause cough? Should I come back if I feel dizzy? Do I need a blood test or a chest x-ray? So many doubts, doctor.

[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): It is commonly combined with a water tablet, yes. Telmisartan very rarely causes this kind of cough. If you feel dizzy, sit down and don't drive, and ring us. I will arrange a kidney function and electrolyte blood test because we are changing the pressure medicines, and we might do a chest x-ray only if the cough has not settled in three weeks.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks is a long time to wait with this cough, no? What if it becomes worse before that, or if I bring up blood?

[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the cough worsens, or you cough up blood, or you get fever or true breathlessness, come sooner, do not wait the three weeks. Otherwise I will see you in three weeks to check the pressure and the cough.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will make sure he stops the ramipril and starts the new one. Should we bring the old strips next time so you can see the water tablet name?
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, please bring the water tablet strip or the box next visit so we can name it properly. That would help.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, we will bring the strip. And my knees, you didn't give anything for the knees. Is walking still allowed? I don't want the pressure to rise if I sit all day.

[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): Walking forty minutes is fine, keep it up, it helps the pressure. I am not adding a pain tablet for the knees today. If the knee pain limits you we can look at it another time.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): One last thing, doctor. The Crocin, can I still take it with telmisartan? I get worried mixing tablets.

[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, the Crocin, which is paracetamol, is fine alongside telmisartan and your other tablets, at the five hundred milligram dose when you need it. Reception will give you the blood test form and the three week appointment.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
